about.title: Palmdale Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Palmdale is home to more than 158,000 people, and most of them will sit in an exam room, urgent care, or hospital bed at some point without a second thought. Usually that trust is well placed. Sometimes it isn't, and a missed diagnosis, a wrong dose, or a surgical mistake changes a life in this Los Angeles County city for good. Medical malpractice in California is its own category of claim, governed by a law called MICRA. It sets a short clock: generally one year from the date you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. Before a lawsuit can be filed, the provider must receive 90 days' written notice. Almost every case also needs a qualified medical expert to explain what a careful provider would have done differently. Keep in mind that a poor result, on its own, is not malpractice; the question is whether the standard of care was breached. Our team can help you find the answers you need.

items.title: MICRA's deadlines are short and easy to miss
items.desc: California generally allows one year from discovery and no more than three years from the injury, plus a 90-day notice before filing. We can pin down which dates apply to you before time runs out.

items.title: Expert review is nearly always required
items.desc: Most California malpractice claims cannot move forward without a qualified medical expert. Our team knows how to find and work with the right specialists.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Your initial case review is free, and we work on contingency. You owe nothing unless we recover for you.

items.question: I was treated after a crash on Palmdale Boulevard and my injury got worse. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: Not automatically. Palmdale saw 815 injury collisions in 2025, and plenty of those patients had complicated recoveries that no provider could have prevented. Malpractice means a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that failure caused additional harm. Our team, usually with a medical expert, can sort out whether your worsening was avoidable.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Under MICRA, the general rule is one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, and never more than three years from the injury itself. You must also give the provider 90 days' notice before filing suit. Because these periods overlap in tricky ways, it is wise to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled differently. We can explain how the cap applies to your specific circumstances.
